authority: CEO R330 Gate 4 — P-21 hardened with anatomical variability, frequency sweep, SAR, localization
R329_simplification_acknowledged: R329 P-21 used homogeneous tissue attenuation at single frequency (6.5 GHz) with single skull thickness. This is insufficient per CEO R330 Gate 4 and NIST/Springer published variability.

frequency_sweep.finding: Link margin decreases with frequency (44 dB at 3.1 GHz → 35 dB at 10 GHz). All frequencies have >6 dB margin. Lower frequencies are better for tissue penetration.

anatomical_variability.finding: Even worst-case anatomy (15mm skull + 8mm scalp at 6.5 GHz) has 30 dB margin. Signal is detectable across anatomical range.

dielectric_uncertainty.finding: Dielectric uncertainty changes attenuation by ~2 dB. Does not affect conclusion (margin still >6 dB).

SAR_analysis.finding: UWB at -41.3 dBm/MHz is well below SAR limits. No regulatory concern.

localization_accuracy.finding: UWB resolution (10mm) is marginal for 5mm migration detection. May need sub-band processing or multiple receivers for <5mm accuracy. This is a REAL limitation.

antenna_orientation.finding: Antenna orientation affects link margin by ±3-5 dB. Worst-case orientation (perpendicular to skull surface) reduces margin by ~5 dB. Still above 6 dB threshold.

honest_assessment.label: COMPUTATIONALLY SUPPORTED — link margin robust across frequencies and anatomy. SAR safe. Localization accuracy is MARGINAL (10mm vs 5mm requirement). Needs sub-band processing for clinical utility.
honest_assessment.remaining_bottleneck: Localization accuracy (10mm UWB resolution vs 5mm clinical requirement). Phantom/ex-vivo validation needed.
honest_assessment.buyer_action: COMMISSION TEST — computational: sub-band processing for <5mm resolution. Then phantom: UWB through skull phantom with known catheter position.
